relations.statement: i = j ∘ f and j = i ∘ g
relations.hypotheses: i : P -> C and j : Q -> C injective; f : P -> Q and g : Q -> P supplied

relations.statement: g ∘ f = id_P and f ∘ g = id_Q

lemmas.statement: For f : P -> Q and g : Q -> P, there exist injective i : P -> C and j : Q -> C with i = j ∘ f and j = i ∘ g iff g ∘ f = id and f ∘ g = id.
lemmas.lean_skeleton: theorem faithful_descent_iff_round_trip_coherent {P Q : Type} (f : P → Q) (g : Q → P) : (∃ (C : Type) (i : P → C) (j : Q → C), Function.Injective i ∧ Function.Injective j ∧ i = j ∘ f ∧ j = i ∘ g) ↔ (g ∘ f = id ∧ f ∘ g = id) := by sorry

lemmas.statement: Given injective i, j with i = j∘f and j = i∘g, we get i∘g∘f = i and j∘f∘g = j; cancelling injective maps gives g∘f = id and f∘g = id.
lemmas.lean_skeleton: theorem faithful_descent_to_coherent {P Q C : Type} (f : P → Q) (g : Q → P) (i : P → C) (j : Q → C) (hi : Function.Injective i) (hj : Function.Injective j) (h1 : i = j ∘ f) (h2 : j = i ∘ g) : g ∘ f = id ∧ f ∘ g = id := by sorry

near_misses.claim: Only g ∘ f = id suffices for a faithful common carrier
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: The target requires both equations i = j∘f and j = i∘g; the second cancellation needs f ∘ g = id_Q as well.

near_misses.claim: Dropping injectivity of i or j still yields round-trip coherence
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: Cancellation requires injectivity; a constant map to a point satisfies the identifying equations for any f, g.
